content:
It's another new week, and another streaming service has hiked its prices. ESPN announced this week that both ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited are raising their fees simultaneously, with some Disney+ and Hulu bundle plans also seeing price increases.

The price hike was discovered by Sports Media Watch via ESPN's support pages, with the new pricing taking effect on September 17. Details are as follows:

  • ESPN Select monthly: USD 14/month (previously USD 13/month)
  • ESPN Select annual: USD 140/year (previously USD 130/year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly: USD 32/month (previously USD 30/month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual: USD 320/year (previously USD 300/year)

According to reports, this is ESPN's first price increase since it restructured its streaming strategy last year.

At the same time, some Disney-related bundle plans have also raised their prices in line with ESPN's streaming service increase.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select: USD 22/month (previously USD 20/month)
  • Disney+ (without ads), Hulu (without ads) and ESPN Select: USD 33/month (previously USD 30/month)

According to The Verge, the price hike also affects the legacy ad-free Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select bundle plan, which is no longer accepting new subscribers, with the monthly fee rising from USD 25 to USD 28.

The good news is that ESPN Unlimited-related bundle plans are not affected by this price increase.

Peacock also announced a price hike last week, with monthly fees going up by up to USD 3 and annual fees by up to USD 30. Apple has also recently raised prices for Apple Music and Apple One.
